items.heading: For Years, the Only Visible
items.text: For years, the only visible way into this space looked like starting a channel and hoping it grew. That is no longer the honest picture. India's creator economy is now supported by a real job market, and roughly 60% of creator-related hiring sits outside influencer-facing titles altogether, spanning video production, community management, and content operations, according to Indeed data covered by Business Standard.

figures.label: Wider Creator Ecosystem Influences Somewhere
figures.source: BCG estimated in 2025 that India already has 2-2.5 million monetized creators, and that the wider creator ecosystem influences somewhere between $350-400 billion in consumer spending, money moving through brand deals, commerce-linked content, and platform advertising that did not flow this way a decade ago. India's influencer marketing spend specifically grew to around ₹4,500 crore in 2025, up from roughly ₹3,600 crore the year before.

figures.label: India's GDP 2024 Supported 930
figures.source: One platform alone shows how large the supporting economy has become. YouTube's creative ecosystem contributed more than ₹16,000 crore to India's GDP in 2024 and supported over 930,000 full-time equivalent jobs, according to Oxford Economics research reported by Business Standard. That is not 930,000 people making videos, most of those jobs sit in editing, production, marketing, agency support, and the businesses built to serve the platform's creators.
